title: AOPedex: AOP-based endocrine disruption extrapolation as white-box mechanism maps for zero-data species
abstract: Endocrine disruption evidence is concentrated in a handful of model species, leaving risk assessment for ‘zero-data species’ unresolved; scarce toxicity records and biologically untraceable black-box extrapolation constrain machine learning. We present AOPedex, a knowledge-driven white-box framework embedding ToxCast in vitro activity, receptor binding-pocket conservation and traceable close-relative evidence in a deterministic AOP event-network propagation skeleton, so that mechanistic maps share one source for prediction, attribution and audit.

title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
abstract: We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: AI-Based Monitoring Devices for the Identification of Circadian Parameters as Digital Predictive Biomarkers of Neurodegenerative Diseases in Older Adults: Systematic Review.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, and related dementias are a growing health burden among older adults. Circadian disruption is increasingly recognized as both a consequence and a potential early marker of neurodegenerative progression. Wearable sensing combined with AI enables continuous, noninvasive, and ecologically valid monitoring of circadian parameters as potential digital biomarkers.

title: Materials chemist and nanoscientist George Whitesides dies at 87
abstract: From organic synthesis to low-cost diagnostics, this prolific researcher explored a broad range of chemistry

title: LCatlas: A Point-Of-Care Tool for Predicting Immunotherapy Outcomes in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, with a minority of patients experiencing durable responses to first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Currently, there are no easily accessible tools to predict clinical benefit to first-line immunotherapy. To address this gap, we developed LCatlas (https://www.lcatlas.org), a point-of-care web application designed to predict immunotherapy outcomes and inform evidence-based treatment decisions.

title: Machine learning-based risk prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B: current evidence and future directions.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and the risk persists despite potent nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Current surveillance relies on broad clinical categories and conventional risk scores, although HCC risk in CHB is heterogeneous and changes over time. This review summarizes current approaches to HCC risk stratification in CHB, critically appraises machine learning (ML)-based models for individualized prediction, and discusses requirements for clinical implementation.

title: Single-cell transcriptome-based identification of core keratinocyte biomarkers and targeted drug discovery for atopic dermatitis.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disorder driven by epidermal barrier impairment and keratinocyte dysfunction. Current therapies are limited by insufficient target specificity and high recurrence rates. This study aimed to identify keratinocyte-derived biomarkers and develop novel targeted agents for precise diagnosis and treatment of AD.

abstract: Company reports 6% reduction in steam use, but full savings remain uncertain

title: Q&A: Making hydrogen peroxide without using precious metals
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide is used in many industrial processes, with several million tons of it being manufactured worldwide every year. Whereas the standard production method requires rare precious metals, chemists from Rutgers University–Newark in the US and the University of Bonn have now described an alternative technique that does away with these metals, making it potentially cheaper and more sustainable. Their findings have now been published in the journal Nature Communications. In the following interview, the authors describe the technology.

title: OMIGAT: Multi-Feature Enhanced Collaborative Attention and Graph Convolution Model for Cancer Driver Gene Identification.
abstract: Human cancers encompass a diverse spectrum of malignancies characterized by extensive molecular diversity, heterogeneous biological behaviors, and distinct evolutionary trajectories. The identification and characterization of cancer driver genes (CDGs) constitute a critical step toward advancing precision oncology and individualized treatment. However, noise interference in multi-omics data, the incompleteness of prior biological networks, and complex topological structures constrain the predictive performance of existing deep learning models.

title: Cathode Surface Reconfiguration via Solvent Chemistry for Durable All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
abstract: Electrode surfaces and interfaces critically dominate the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, established additive-oriented strategies physically isolate the cathode from the electrolyte without improving the restricted Li+ transport pathways of the cathode surface. Here, we propose a solvation-mediated chemical etching mechanism governing cathode surface reconfiguration, driven by competition between solvent coordination and lattice stabilization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Cyclopropenimine Ligands: Coordination Chemistry and Catalytic Applications
abstract: Cyclopropenimines (CPIs) are a class of structurally modular, neutral nitrogen donors in which strong electron donation is coupled to charge redistribution and aromatic stabilization within the cyclopropenium framework. This perspective examines the emerging coordination chemistry and catalytic applications of CPI ligands, with emphasis on how their electronic structure underpins diverse bonding interactions with transition metal and main group centers.

title: Symmetry-Breaking Charge Localization Controls Radiationless Decay in a Multibranched Charge-Transfer State
abstract: Symmetry breaking in multibranched charge-transfer (CT) excited states is generally viewed as a mechanism for excited-state localization, yet how such localization controls the subsequent fate of the excitation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that environmental stabilization of a symmetry-broken CT state can fundamentally reshape radiationless decay in a bent donor–acceptor–donor chromophore.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Efficient and Low-Impact Enzymatic Glycosylation with Robust Sucrose Synthase Variants
abstract: Glycosyltransferase-driven glycosylation enables environmentally mild synthesis of high-value chemicals, but industrial implementation is constrained by the cost of UDP-glucose. Sucrose synthase (SuSy) offers an attractive route for UDP-glucose recycling, yet inadequate operational stability has limited its use. Here, we report an integrated engineering workflow that overcomes the longstanding trade-off between efficiency and robustness in glycosyl donor recycling enzymes. We engineered GmSuSy wild-type and obtained variants combining supra-wild-type activity (178%) with enhanced thermostability (ΔTmapp = 13.3 °C), solvent tolerance (70% retained activity in 25% DMSO), and a 123-fold longer half-life. The variants achieved estimated theoretical total turnover numbers of up to ∼10 million (60 °C), supporting their industrial relevance. Mechanistic analyses revealed that long-range residue communication networks couple oligomeric interfaces with active sites, shifting conformational populations toward stable, catalytically competent states, while increasing hydrophobic packing and reducing solvent accessibility. This enhanced robustness enabled significant process-level gains, including >90% conversion yields in indoxyl and methyl anthranilate glycosylation. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate the potential to halve reaction costs and reduce environmental impacts threefold, establishing SuSy robustness as a key lever for industrial glycosylation.

title: Transition-Metal-Mediated Discharge Intermediates Set Anionic-Redox Potentials and Voltage Hysteresis in Li-Rich Cathodes
abstract: Voltage hysteresis arising from anionic redox reactions remains a central bottleneck for lithium-rich cathodes. While ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been invoked to describe the charging pathway, its proposed reverse counterpart, metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), remains experimentally unresolved during discharge. Here, using cation-disordered rock-salt Li2Ni0.33Ta0.66O3 (LNTO) as a model system, we combine electrochemical relaxation analysis with synchrotron-based spectroscopy to identify, for the first time, a metastable reduction intermediate characterized by…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Composition-Only Descriptor for Predicting Single-Phase High-Entropy Perovskite Oxides
abstract: High-entropy perovskite oxides (HEPOs) offer a vast compositional space through multicomponent substitution across the A and B sites of the ABO3 framework, but identifying which compositions form single-phase perovskites still relies on trial-and-error synthesis or per-composition computation, slowing materials discovery. Here, we propose a composition-only phase-formation descriptor, η, developed for equimolar five-component A-site systems, (A1A2A3A4A5)TiO3, by combining machine-learned-potential stability evaluations with synthesis and X-ray diffraction (XRD) labels.

title: Phosphate selectivity in XPR1 is driven by direct multi-ion competition
abstract: Inorganic phosphate (Pi) is essential for numerous cellular processes, and its intracellular concentration must be tightly regulated. In mammals, phosphate efflux is mediated by the Xenotropic and Polytropic Retrovirus Receptor 1 (XPR1/SLC53A1), the only known mammalian Pi exporter. We and others have recently proposed that XPR1 functions like a Pi channel, with the protein preferentially conducting the H2PO4- species of Pi over HPO42-. While some studies suggest that XPR1 can conduct other anions, the molecular basis of XPR1 substrate selectivity remains unknown. Here, we use over 110 s of molecular dynamics simulations, together with free-energy calculations, to investigate substrate selectivity in XPR1. We show that H2PO4- (Pi1-) is preferentially conducted over HPO42- (Pi2-), and that Pi1- progressively outcompetes Cl- for occupancy of the transport pathway. Free-energy and ion-interaction analyses reveal that selectivity arises from two distinct mechanisms: favourable protein-Pi interactions and direct ion-ion interactions in the pore. This direct contact facilitates Pi1- displacement via the previously proposed knock-kiss-kick mechanism, whereas entry of Cl- is restricted due to the preference for water-mediated interactions. Simulations with additional anions show that XPR1 remains permissive to several monovalent species, including nitrate, bicarbonate and methanesulfonate, while poorly conducting the divalent anion sulfate. These findings suggest that XPR1 does not achieve phosphate selectivity through absolute exclusion of competing anions. Instead, preferential Pi transport emerges from substrate-specific interactions and competition between multiple ions within a relatively permissive permeation pathway, providing a molecular basis for substrate discrimination in XPR1.

title: Taming Metal–Electrolyte Interface via Two-Dimensional Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Behavioral Plasticity and Dispersal of Free Swimming Coral Larvae via Vertical Tracking Microscopy
abstract: Coral larvae disperse and seek suitable sites for settlement while undergoing rapid development, making this period central to reef connectivity, recruitment, and recovery. Yet how the accompanying changes in larval morphology, ciliary activity, and swimming behavior shape dispersal remains poorly understood. Here, using vertical tracking microscopy, we follow individual Acropora millepora larvae over hundreds of body lengths at successive developmental stages while resolving body morphology. We show a developmental progression from buoyant rise to upward- and downward-directed gravitactic swimming, followed by weaker gravitactic alignment at later stages, accompanied by body elongation and increasingly structured ciliary flows. Integrating these kinematics into a minimal, data-driven model, we separate buoyant drift from active swimming and estimate the propulsion costs of vertical migration and lateral spreading. Buoyancy supports early ascent without propulsion expenditure, while the model predicts lower costs of descent and lateral spreading at late developmental stages. Simulations in fluctuating flow, assuming no flow sensing, predict that directed swimming weakens when flow-induced rotation acts on timescales comparable to intrinsic heading relaxation. Together, these results reveal how development reorganizes the physical drivers of larval motion in ways that may support the transition from dispersal to settlement, providing a basis for incorporating developmental changes in swimming into models of coral larval dispersal.

title: Closed-loop navigation of reaction-diffusion pattern via Reservoir Computing and electric field modulation
abstract: Inspired by bioelectricity as a principle spanning from cell–cell communication to morphological pattern formation, we developed a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)–based control platform which can electrically navigate self--organizing reaction--diffusion patterns toward target features. The platform implements closed-loop adaptive control integrating real-time monitoring of the controlled system, extraction of visual features from the monitored data, computation of external electrical perturbations using an RNN, and modulation of reaction–diffusion dynamics through electric field actuation.

title: Predicting degradation of polymeric materials in complex chemical environments via molecular modeling
abstract: This Perspective explores how physical models, in collaboration with big data and artificial intelligence, can accelerate our understanding of the degradation of soft materials.

title: Sodium coordination at the Na2 site enforces ion-substrate coupling in serotonin transporter SERT
abstract: Secondary active transporters use the thermodynamically favorable movement of an ion down its electrochemical gradient to drive substrate accumulation against a concentration gradient. For the human serotonin transporter (SERT), strict coupling between Na and 5-HT transport is essential for maintaining neurotransmitter homeostasis, yet the structural mechanism by which Na binding enforces this coupling is incompletely understood. Here, we identify an interaction network through which Na coordination at the cation site Ct2 (also known as Na2) modulates conformational change on both sides of the transporter. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that Na occupancy of Ct2 stabilizes specific interactions between residues in TM5, TM8, and TM1 that together gate aqueous access to the cytoplasmic and extracellular pathways. Disruption of this network through mutations at Ct2 residues Asp437 and Ser438, or at the TM5 residue Thr284, reduces the concentrative power of SERT and allows a constitutive Na conductance, consistent with uncoupled Na uniport. These findings reveal how structural integrity at and around the Ct2 site enforces obligatory Na-5-HT coupling and thereby sustains the thermodynamic efficiency of serotonin uptake.

title: ppGpp regulates NAD-RNA decapping by Escherichia coli NudC and RppH
abstract: The regulatory landscape of RNA includes diverse non-canonical 5' cap structures, including Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD+). In E. coli, the NAD cap and its cognate decapping enzyme NudC have provided important insight into NAD+-capped RNA stability; however, broader regulatory control of NAD-capped RNA degradation has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the E. coli Nudix hydrolase RppH, known to act on 5' triphosphorylated RNA, also functions as an NAD+-decapping enzyme.

title: Extraframework Cations Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
abstract: Removal of ultratrace alkynes to produce polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is an important but extremely challenging task. Here, we report a dual-cation strategy in FAU-type zeolites that enables the unprecedented capture of acetylene at concentrations of parts per million (ppm). The optimized Ni–Ba–Y adsorbent delivers high dynamic uptakes of 0.37–0.82 mmol·g–1 at acetylene concentrations of 500–10,000 ppm, with acetylene/ethylene selectivity exceeding 100 under industrial relevant conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Ferrielectric Phase in Tetragonal Tungsten Bronzes with Competing Polar and Antipolar Modes
abstract: Tungsten bronzes represent one of the most important ferroelectric families after perovskites, and the unique dielectric nature has gathered rising scientific interest from both fields of physics and materials science, while the physical understanding on ferroelectric transition and its structure origins remains the crucial issue. Competing polar and antipolar modes play important roles in ferroelectric transition, and antipolar modes are normally suppressed upon cooling, triggering a para-to-ferroelectric transition.

title: Quantitative Steric Hindrance to Determine Pressure-Induced Emission Harvesting.
abstract: Pressure engineering enables distinctive pressure-induced emission (PIE) and piezochromism in halide perovskites, yet structural reversibility generally prevents ambient condition retention of high-pressure metastable states (HPMS), limiting their practical optoelectronic applications. This perspective compares PIE retention behavior across all-inorganic, aliphatic-cation, and aromatic-cation hybrid halide perovskites.

title: Strong Metal–Support Interaction in Ag/TiO2 Breaks the Activity–Selectivity Trade-off in Photocatalytic Oxidative Coupling of Methane
abstract: Photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) is a promising route for the direct conversion of methane into value-added hydrocarbons, yet it is fundamentally limited by the trade-off between methane activation and overoxidation. Herein, we report that the strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) effect in Ag/TiO2 breaks this activity–selectivity trade-off, enabling high-performance continuous-flow OCM.

title: Concerted Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Absorption and Localized Photoluminescence in an Fe(III) Photosensitizer
abstract: There is tremendous interest in the electronic structure of [FeIII(phtmeimb)2]+, the first iron complex to show room temperature photoluminescence (PL) with an excited-state lifetime sufficient for dynamic quenching in fluid solution. Two types of excited states are generated by light absorption, termed the Franck–Condon (FC) state and the thermally equilibrated excited state (THEXI) that is photoluminescent. Herein we report solvatochromic and electroabsorption studies to probe the electronic structure of these two states.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: TCDD-Induced m⁶A Profiling Identifies SUV39H2 as a Positive Regulator of Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Signaling
abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) mediates cellular responses to environmental contaminants, including 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD). Although AHR-dependent transcriptional regulation is well characterized, the contributions of RNA modifications and chromatin-associated regulators to AHR signaling remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated TCDD-associated changes in N-methyladenosine (mA) RNA modification and identified suppressor of variegation 3-9 homolog 2 (SUV39H2) as a previously unrecognized positive regulator of AHR signaling. Exploratory methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) and matched RNA-seq analyses were performed in vehicle- and TCDD-treated HepG2 cells, followed by independent molecular and functional validation. TCDD increased mA enrichment and mRNA stability of canonical AHR-responsive transcripts, including CYP1A1, CYP1A2, and AHRR, accompanied by increased gene expression. Notably, SUV39H2 was identified as a TCDD-responsive mA-enriched transcript exhibiting increased mRNA stability and protein expression without a substantial change in steady-state mRNA abundance. Functional studies demonstrated that SUV39H2 depletion and pharmacological inhibition attenuated TCDD-induced AHR target gene expression and transcriptional activity, whereas SUV39H2 overexpression enhanced AHR-dependent responses. CUT&RUN-qPCR analyses further implicated SUV39H2 in AHR-associated transcriptional regulation at the CYP1A1 enhancer. Consistent with the cellular findings, pharmacological inhibition of SUV39H2 attenuated TCDD-induced expression of AHR-responsive genes in mouse liver. Collectively, these findings identify SUV39H2 as a previously unrecognized positive regulator of AHR signaling and suggest that TCDD-associated mA modification and mRNA stabilization contribute to the regulation of AHR-responsive transcripts and chromatin-associated regulatory factors.

title: In Situ STEM Imaging of Colloidal Crystals Based on Programmable Atom Equivalents
abstract: It is challenging to image the assembly of colloidal crystals composed of programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) using electron microscopy (EM). PAEs typically consist of nanoparticle cores densely functionalized with radially oriented DNA shells, which assemble in the liquid phase via DNA bonds. EM requires high-vacuum conditions, and electron beams can damage soft materials like nucleic acids.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Improving Target-Adverse Event Association Prediction via Inverse Node Frequency Transformation to Mitigate Knowledge Graph Topological Bias
abstract: Motivation: Identifying significant associations between therapeutic protein targets and adverse events (AEs) is a critical component of drug safety assessment. To accelerate the process, machine learning methods have been developed to predict these associations as edges in network data integrating molecular interactions and other key biomedical knowledge. However, these networks often suffer from topological imbalances where a minority of "hub" nodes determine the predictive signal.

title: Aryl Palladium Acetates as Highly Active Species in Intermolecular Heck Reactions of Hindered Olefins
abstract: Despite decades of development since the early 1970s, the intermolecular Heck reaction of hindered tri- and tetrasubstituted olefins with aryl halides has remained a challenge. Traditional approaches relied on rate-acceleration by directing groups or high reactivity of cationic arylpalladium species generated from triflates and diazonium salts. Herein, we report the first general and efficient Heck coupling between trisubstituted alkenes (and selected tetrasubstituted olefins) with aryl iodides and bromides.

title: Structure of Wadsley−Roth Nb14W3O44 and Response to High-Rate Lithium Insertion and Extraction with Links to Negative Thermal Expansion
abstract: Wadsley−Roth crystallographic shear structures are intrinsically hierarchical compounds comprising blocks of corner-sharing octahedra that are isolated by shear planes. Nb14W3O44 is the (4 × 4)1 member of a homologous series of niobium tungsten oxide Wadsley−Roth structures. Nb14W3O44 and other Wadsley−Roth compounds exhibit unusually rapid intercalation chemistry and interesting structural responses such as non-monotonic lattice changes during lithium insertion and extraction, but there are unexplored questions regarding the rate dependence of the structure evolution or possible correlations…

title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
abstract: Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

title: An Organocatalytic Borrowing Hydrogen Reaction by Flavin Photocatalyst
abstract: Borrowing hydrogen (BH) reactions offer an atom-economical and green pathway to build complex molecules using abundantly available and inexpensive alcohols as alkylating agents. However, major BH catalysts comprise transition metals, employing decorated ligands and require high reaction temperatures. A full BH cycle using an organocatalyst operating under mild reaction conditions attracts significant attention but remains elusive.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Atroposelective Hydroaminocarbonylation of Alkynes: Access to Axially Chiral Amides
abstract: Despite significant advances in asymmetric carbonylation, the construction of open-chain axially chiral styrenes remains elusive, primarily due to their high conformational flexibility and inherently low rotational barriers. Here, we present a copper-catalyzed atroposelective hydroaminocarbonylation of internal alkynes that directly accesses axially chiral amides. This transformation employs a copper hydride catalytic system with CO and O-benzoyl hydroxylamines, operating under mild conditions to deliver products with good regio- and enantioselectivity. The reaction demonstrates practical utility, tolerating a range of functional groups and accommodating some bioactive derivatives. Furthermore, thermal studies confirm the low rotational barriers of the resulting amides, underscoring the challenge successfully overcome by this methodology.

title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC.

title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys.
abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy-interstitial diffusivity convergence.

title: Elucidating the Iron Effect in Alkaline Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Structural Transformation, Dynamic Synergy, and Industrial Realities
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is critical for carbon neutrality, but its efficiency is significantly limited by the kinetically slow oxygen evolution reaction (OER). While earth-abundant 3d transition-metal catalysts are promising alternatives, their exceptional performance is strongly associated with the prominent Fe effect. The electrocatalysis community remains divided by prolonged scientific discussion regarding whether Fe functions as a direct active site or a passive electronic spectator.

title: Boosting Photocatalytic Hydrogen Production from Simulated Seawater via a Double S-Scheme Heterojunction: The Pivotal Role of Oxygen-Deficient TiO2 as a Charge Recombination Hub-DFT Study
abstract: Hydrogen production via seawater splitting using solar energy is a sustainable and promising approach to address the ever-growing energy crisis. However, the various ions present in seawater inhibit photocatalytic performance through photocorrosion, fouling, and active-site blockage. Therefore, designing a robust, stable, and durable photocatalyst is necessary.
