A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells
abstract: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb.

title: Metal-Dependent Oxygen Evolution at Interfaces Derived from Structure-Matched Iron and Nickel Self-Assembled Monolayers (SAMs)
abstract: Understanding the fundamental differences in activity between iron- and nickel-based catalysts in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) has been complicated by the structural complexity of traditional heterogeneous systems. To disentangle intrinsic metal effects, a series of simple, precisely structurally defined molecular models with controlled coordination environments was prepared and employed in water oxidation catalysis (WOC).

title: MolCodon: A Codon-Based Molecular Language for Interpretable Structural Representation and Similarity Search
abstract: Molecular representation determines which aspects of chemical structure can be learned, compared, and interpreted in computational drug discovery. Existing encodings typically emphasize either compact string description, as in SMILES and SELFIES, or efficient similarity search, as in circular fingerprints. Although canonical SMILES already provides a deterministic string, its tokens are variable in width and carry no fixed chemical role. No existing representation simultaneously offers fixed-width, role-assigned tokenization, graph-level interpretability, pharmacophore annotation, and high-fidelity molecular reconstruction. Here, we introduce MolCodon, a codon-based molecular language that represents small molecules as deterministic sequences of fixed-width three-character tokens over a five-symbol alphabet, C, N, O, S, and X. Inspired by the triplet organization of the genetic code, MolCodon assigns chemically defined codon families to atoms, bonds, ring and branch topology, fused-ring references, pharmacophore features, bond mobility, charge, and stereochemistry. A deterministic graph traversal with ring-contiguity preservation produces sequences in which chemically meaningful substructures remain locally organized and traceable to the underlying molecular graph. Across approximately 2.9 million molecules from six commercial screening libraries, MolCodon achieved 98.93% InChIKey-level round-trip fidelity, supporting its use as a high-fidelity sequence representation for drug-like compounds. Across ten QSAR tasks, MolCodon-derived sparse sequence and trace features showed statistically supported advantages over the SMILES and SELFIES-based representations in most data sets while achieving competitive performance with classical fingerprints. These findings are supported by five repeated cross-validation and Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons. As an application of the representation, the MolCodon similarity engine decomposes molecular similarity into ring topology, branch context, attachment architecture, and pharmacophore correspondence, enabling interpretable scaffold-hopping searches. In a PARP1 virtual screening case study, MolCodon retrieved scaffold-diverse candidates using a known PARP-1 inhibitor Olaparib as the template compound. Together, these results establish MolCodon as a new molecular representation paradigm that transforms chemical graphs into high-fidelity, interpretable, and alignment-compatible codon sequences, opening a direct path for bioinformatics-inspired analysis of small-molecule chemical space. The MolCodon encoder, decoder, and similarity engine are freely available as open-source software at https://github.com/DurdagiLab/MolCodon.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A deep-learning predictive model for Cas12a activity in wheat
abstract: CRISPR technology has created targeted DNA mutations across the tree of life. Target sites are defined by RNA molecules that largely determine the efficiency of an experiment. Several predictive models are available to select the most efficient RNAs. Unfortunately, these models are not built with plant data and have limited predictive power in plant systems. To overcome this limitation, we established a high-throughput arrayed wheat protoplast transfection method and measured the editing efficiency of ~1,000 unique LbCas12a crRNAs at on- and off-target sites. We trained different models by testing 40 deep learning architectures and found that a convolutional neural network model called 2CaP-5 displayed the best performance. While 2CaP-5 had moderate to strong predictive power in protoplasts, it did not generalize to Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Despite this limitation, we demonstrate that 2CaP-5 can be re-trained with as few as 500 crRNAs. The use of such a small training set is advantageous for low-throughput experimental systems such as typically found in transgenic plant systems. We also used ~2,000 off-targets in the wheat subgenomes to investigate Cas12a specificity. Our dataset confirms previous observations regarding off-targets, specifically that single mismatches reduce indel efficiency provided they are adjacent to the PAM and that off-target activity can be largely prevented by three mismatches. Altogether, our results show that the 2CaP-5 model has moderate to strong predictive power for Cas12a crRNAs in wheat protoplasts and will serve as a useful foundation for predictive tools in other plant species.

title: Radical Molecular-Junction Covalent Organic Framework for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
abstract: Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Allosteric Control and Glycan Shielding Adaptations in the SARS-CoV-2 Spike from Early to Peak Virulence
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 Spike glycoprotein is central to viral infectivity and immune evasion, making it a key target for vaccine and therapeutic design. This trimeric peplomer undergoes dynamic conformational changes, particularly in its Receptor Binding Domain (RBD), which transitions between closed (down) and ACE2-accessible (up) states relative to the rest of the protein, to facilitate host cell entry. Structural understanding of such critical interdomain motions, as well as epitope exposure quantification, is essential for obtaining an effective biochemical handle over this protein and, in turn, exploiting it toward improved immunogen development. Focusing on the early circulating D614G form and the later emerging Delta (B.1.617.2) variant with higher virulence, we performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of the soluble form of the Spike in both “down” and “up” conformations of the RBD. Guided by differences in domain-scale fluctuations, we constructed targeted reaction coordinates capturing NTD and RBD rotations and tilting motions, enabling variant-specific structural distinctions to be quantitatively extracted. Conformational landscape mapping and principal component analysis (PCA) reveal a previously uncharacterized dynamic coupling between the NTD and RBD, wherein tilting motions of the NTD are coupled to RBD gating on the neighboring protomer. While several elements of this interdomain coupling are conserved, the Delta variant exhibits a more constrained and functionally optimized RBD-up conformation that favors ACE2 engagement. Concurrently, Delta-specific mutations restructure NTD-local glycans to enhance shielding of the immunogenic supersite, diminishing neutralizing antibody accessibility. Finally, the D950N substitution at the heptad repeat HR1 helix reshapes long-range interactions and alters bending/twisting dynamics of the Spike stalk, likely contributing to both fusion efficiency and immune evasion. Together, these simulations uncover chemically encoded strategies of variant adaptation─through long-range allostery, glycan repositioning, and conformational bias─that shape Spike structure and function. These biochemical and structural insights offer valuable guidance for rational vaccine and therapeutic design against SARS-CoV-2 and emerging variants.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Synthesis of Cellulose Nanofiber Hydrogel Beads from Typha angustifolia for the Immobilization of Protease
abstract: Typha angustifolia, an invasive aquatic macrophyte, poses a persistent challenge to wetland and irrigation management, yet its cellulose-rich biomass represents an underexploited feedstock for value-added biomaterials. This study reports the synthesis of cellulose nanofiber (CNF) hydrogel beads from T. angustifolia and evaluates their performance as a support matrix for protease immobilization. Cellulose was isolated by chlorite delignification and alkaline treatment, oxidized with sodium periodate to introduce aldehyde functional groups, blended with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and crosslinked with glutaraldehyde to form hydrogel beads. The beads exhibited a high water-absorption capacity of 399.67 {plus minus} 0.53% and a mechanical strength of 1.27 MPa. Covalent immobilization of crude protease onto the beads increased specific activity nearly threefold, from 24.56 {plus minus} 0.39 U/mg for the free enzyme to 59.20 {plus minus} 1.06 U/mg for the immobilized enzyme, corresponding to a loading efficiency of 50.61%. The immobilized enzyme also displayed broadened thermal and pH optima, shifting from 40 {degree sign}C to 50 {degree sign}C and from pH 8.0 to 9.0, respectively, and an extended operational half-life from 4.40 h to 11.37 h. These findings support the valorization of invasive Typha biomass into a robust, biodegradable support system with potential application in industrial biocatalysis.

title: Evaluating Boltz-2 prediction of mutation-induced protein–ligand affinity changes
abstract: Protein mutations can affect how a protein binds a ligand and this may contribute to drug resistance as well as variability in patient responses to treatment. However, experimentally measuring binding affinities across numerous variants in real life is costly. Here we evaluated the accuracy of Boltz-2, a protein computational model used for biomolecular structure and binding-affinity prediction, by using experimentally determined reference-variant protein-ligand pairs collected from four independent data sources under the same experimental conditions.

title: Temporal programming of pH in enzyme-encapsulated artificial cells: role of differential membrane permeability
abstract: Coupling autocatalytic reaction networks and membrane-regulated transport of species within confined compartments provides a powerful strategy for engineering programmable dynamics in artificial cells. Here, we demonstrate temporal control of pH in phospholipid vesicles by encapsulating glucose oxidase (GOx) and urease enzymes, which respectively generate acidic and basic products from glucose and urea.

title: Selectivity for Fe versus Carbonyl Centered Silylation in Low-Valent β-Diketiminate Fe Complexes
abstract: Understanding the changes in reactivity and selectivity engendered by weak-field supporting ligands and multimetallic complexes offers new opportunities in organometallic chemistry. Here, we examine the selectivity of reactions of silyl electrophiles with monometallic iron-carbonyl complexes, which can lead to silylation either at the metal to form a silyl complex, or at a CO ligand to give a carbyne complex. The first mode of reactivity is common with classic organometallic complexes, and the latter has been observed more recently with complexes with strong-field ligands.

title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed Regiodivergent Enantioselective C2- and C4–H Alkylation of Indoles
abstract: Switchable regiodivergent asymmetric synthesis constitutes a powerful paradigm in asymmetric catalysis, which greatly expands synthetic versatility and allows the efficient assembly of structurally diverse chiral molecules. Herein, we report a switchable regiodivergent enantioselective C–H functionalization of indoles with nitroalkenes, delivering a tunable platform to access C2- and C4-functionalized chiral indole derivatives with high efficiency, as well as excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to 97% yield, 96% ee, and >10:1 rr).

title: Isosteres in Chemistry
abstract: Dating back to 1919 with its coinage by Irving Langmuir, isosterism has continuously evolved over the past century. While ever changing, the overall idea has remained constant; isosteres are interchangeable groups or atoms which modulate a compound’s chemical properties. At a fundamental level, understanding the key concepts of isosterism has allowed for the development of a framework which enables intellectual compound design.

title: Preserving Identity in an Ecosystem of Synthetic Cells by Macromolecular Crowding
abstract: To synthesize life from non-living matter, we require, at a minimum, ecosystems of synthetic cells that are capable of adaptive evolution. Such evolution, in turn, requires distinct individuals in an ecosystem to compete for resources so that successful ones can pass on their genotypes, while weaker ones succumb. Fuel-dependent synthetic cells built from complex coacervate droplets offer a route towards such evolution: they emerge when fuel is present, decay when it runs out, and freely exchange nutrients and waste with their surroundings.

title: Models of Cofactors B12 and F430: Can Corrinoids Stabilize Nickel(I)?
abstract: We have examined four sterically constrained corrinoid ligands vis-à-vis their ability to stabilize low-oxidation-state transition metal centers, especially Ni(I), using modern DFT calculations with two exchange-correlation functionals (OLYP-D3 and B3LYP*) and large STO-TZ2P basis sets. The four ligands include a true corrin with a linear 14-p-electron conjugation pathway, a tetradehydrocorrin and an octadehydrocorrin with more extended, 2D conjugation, and a 5,6-dihydrocorrin with a shorter, linear 12-p-electron conjugation pathway.

title: Metal Fluorides as Heterogeneous Base Catalysts: Exceptional C-C Bond Formation Activity from LaF 3
abstract: Metal fluoride surfaces have potential as heterogeneous base catalysts. A systematic evaluation of rare-earth and alkaline-earth fluorides demonstrated the exceptional C-C bond formation activity of LaF 3 , rivaling or exceeding that of Mg-Al hydrotalcite. Hammett and kinetic isotope effect studies identified nitroalkane activation by basic sites as vital to this catalysis.

title: Transducing a CO2 Concentration Gradient into Electrical Energy through Copper–Ethylenediamine Coordination
abstract: A gas-phase concentration gradient contains Gibbs free energy, while converting this energy into electricity requires a chemical transduction mechanism. Here, we convert a CO2 concentration gradient into a Cu redox-potential difference through copper–ethylenediamine coordination. Ethylenediamine (eda) acts as a bifunctional molecular transducer: its coordination stabilizes the Cu2+ state, whereas CO2-induced protonation of eda diminishes coordination ability and stabilizes the metallic Cu.

title: Secondary Organic Aerosol Formation from Cleaning Product Use in a Residential Kitchen
abstract: Secondary organic aerosol (SOA) can form indoors when volatile organic compounds (VOCs), commonly emitted from the use of scented cleaning products and other chemical products, undergo oxidation and condense onto aerosols. Indoor oxidants can come from a variety of sources, including the use of chlorine bleach for surface cleaning and disinfection, operation of germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) lamps for air disinfection, and penetration of ozone (O 3 ) from the outdoor environment.

title: What makes a laboratory self-driving? Mapping the SDL terminology landscape and introducing the FLEx categorization framework
abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are increasingly used to accelerate experimentation across chemistry, materials science, biotechnology, and related fields. Yet, the rapid development of autonomous experimentation has produced a fragmented terminology landscape in which overlapping terms, including autonomous laboratories, materials acceleration platforms, and robot scientists, are applied inconsistently. This complicates comparisons between systems and obscures what constitutes scientific autonomy.

title: Configuration-dependent hydrogen adsorption thermodynamics on S-doped RuO2(110): A first-principles study
abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a promising non-platinum electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet its intrinsic activity is limited by strong hydrogen adsorption on coordinatively unsaturated Ru surface sites.Density functional theory calculations show that substitutional sulfur doping improves the HER adsorption thermodynamics of RuO2(110) by tuning hydrogen adsorption via local environment engineering. S doping weakens excessive hydrogen binding and drives the system toward near-optimal HER thermodynamics, approaching the benchmark ΔGH of Pt[3].

title: Multigram Synthesis of the 1,3-Substituted Cuneane Amino Acids
abstract: Cuneanes are obtained from cubanes in a single step and reproduce the exit vectors of meta- and parasubstituted benzenes, but the corresponding amino acid building blocks have remained unavailable. Herein, we report a preparative route to cuneane amino acids based on the Curtius rearrangement of cuneane halfesters. Both regioisomers of the 1,3-disubstituted series are accessible from the two complementary halfesters: tert-butanol gives the Boc-protected amino esters in 84% and 91% yield on a 10 g scale, and standard operations convert them into the Boc and Fmoc amino acids, the methyl and…

title: Molecular Assembly Enumeration vs. 1D Dictionary Compression Across the Nano-DrugBank Small-Molecule Repository
abstract: Assembly Theory (AT) defines the Molecular Assembly Index (MA) as the minimal number of recursive bonddisjoint subgraph-joining steps required to construct a 2D molecular graph [1, 2, 4], whereas critics from Algorithmic Information Theory (AIT) contend that empirical MA rankings collapse to standard 1D dictionary compression applied to molecular strings [5, 6, 15].

title: ReConLiG: Reaction-Guided Design of Organometallic Ligands via Decoupled Generative Pretraining and Contrastive Alignment
abstract: Ligand design remains a central challenge in organometallic catalysis. Existing generative models rely on predefined molecular descriptors or require extensive labelled data for reaction-specific fine-tuning. We introduce ReConLiG, a framework that uses reaction information directly to generate ligand candidates without predefined target descriptors. ReConLiG decouples ligand generation from reaction guidance. The generative module learns a continuous and chemically interpretable ligand latent space from 500,000 unlabelled Sadphos pseudo-ligands.

title: Reversible photoinduced excimer-like emission in indolocarbazole- derivatives in frozen solutions and host matrixes
abstract: Excimer formation can profoundly affect the emission colour and efficiency of organic optoelectronic devices, yet the mechanisms governing the formation and stability of intermolecular emissive states remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate irradiation-induced changes in the photoluminescence of indolo[3,2,1- jk ]carbazole ( ICz ) and nitrogen-containing ICz derivatives in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran glasses at 77 K and in host–guest films at room temperature.

title: GENESIS: Potency-Graded Contrastive Learning for Generative Molecular Design and Drug Repurposing in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Computational drug discovery typically binarizes bioactivity, discarding the graded doseresponse signal needed for lead prioritization. We introduce Potency-Graded Contrastive Learning (PGCL), projecting frozen molecular language-model embeddings into a 128dimensional space via an ordinal contrastive objective, six-tier negative taxonomy, and tier-margin ranking.

title: Dynamic Aggregation as a Widespread and Reversible Mechanism of Capacity Fade in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: Aqueous organic redox flow batteries (RFBs) promise inexpensive large-scale energy storage for electricity produced from intermittent renewable energy. However, high capacity fade rates in RFBs that use inexpensive redox-active organic molecules (ROMs) represent a major barrier to commercialization. Most capacity fade mechanisms have been attributed to molecular decomposition of ROMs, and their prevention through molecular engineering typically raises the cost of the final battery system.

title: Solvent-Mediated Heat-Shock Trapping of Aromatic Carbonyl Guests in Poly(vinylpyrrolidone) Enables White-light Fluorescence, UV and Green-Light-Excited Red Phosphorescence, Delayed NIR Emission
abstract: Nonequilibrium polymer processing provides a route to generating emissive states without the need to synthesize new covalent chromophores. We report a simple physical method for encapsulating aromatic carbonyl guest molecules within the carbonyl rich polymer poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP). The resulting host-guest systems display guest dependent fluorescence across the visible region with a white light emitting complex being observed for one of the host/guest combinations with CIE coordinates (0.3147, 0.3244), close to the D65 daylight standard and a CCT of approximately 6430 K.

title: Water-Enabled Organic Hydrogenation at Mg-Ni/Co Interface
abstract: Catalytic hydrogenation conventionally relies on precious-metal catalysts such as palladium and platinum together with compressed hydrogen gas, creating cost, safety, and operational constraints. Here we report a hydrogenation platform assembled in situ from abundant metal salts (Ni and Co) and magnesium, generating dynamic metal-magnesium interfaces under ambient conditions.

title: Interfacial Transition-Metal Reduction, Surface Oxygen Depletion and LiNbO 3 Protection in NCM622/Li 6 PS 5 Cl Cathodes Resolved by In Situ Nanoscale XPEEM
abstract: Degradation at the cathode-solid electrolyte interface limits high-energy-density sulfide-based allsolid-state batteries. For Ni-rich LiNi 0.6 Mn 0.2 Co 0.2 O 2 (NCM622), cathode surface reduction and electrolyte oxidation are coupled through interfacial (electro-)chemical reactions. Although LiNbO 3 coatings are known to mitigate interfacial resistance growth, their effect on this coupling during operation remains unclear.

title: Population-Balance Tilt Sampling for Gradient-based Free-Energy Reconstruction
abstract: Gradient-based free-energy surface (FES) reconstruction typically faces a trade-off between the complexity of evaluating instantaneous forces and the systematic bias introduced by local asymmetry in position-based estimators. To overcome these limitations, we introduce population-balance tilt sampling (PBTS), an adaptive method that applies a linear tilt to a symmetric restraining potential and determines the central free-energy derivative by finding the tilt root that equalizes sample populations across the window center.

title: Electric Field-Driven Transitions from Nonclassical to Classical Carbonyls
abstract: Effect of external oriented electric field (OEF) is studied on the chemical bonding of isolated and complexed CO molecules using Density Functional Theory (DFT). Our findings, discussed the course of blue-shift and red-shift during the application of parallel and anti- parallel OEFs, with respect to the C–O bond vector, in isolated and complexed CO molecules. We give answer to a question, ‘Why the influence of electric field is more prominent in causing the red-shift than the blue-shift?’, via the detailed discussion of involved donor-acceptor interactions.

title: Analysis of Halloysite Nanotubes as Nucleating Agents in Chain-Extended Recycled PET Foams
abstract: Halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) are reported as nucleating agents for crystallization and foam cells, but they have not been studied in recycled poly(ethylene terephthalate) (rPET) foams. Two grades differing in surface area (HNT1: 65 m2/g; HNT2: 25 m2/g) and Fe2O3 content (0.14 vs. 1.1 wt.-%) are compounded at 0–1.5 wt.-% into rPET chain-extended with 1 wt.-% Joncryl ADR 4468. Both grades reduce the isothermal crystallization half-time by up to 62 % at an almost unchanged Avrami exponent (n ≈ 2.3–3.0).

title: AutoMeta: LLM Agent-based Automated Meta-Analysis in Public Health
abstract: Background: Meta-analysis supports public health decision-making, yet conducting and updating reviews remain time- and labour-intensive. Although large language model (LLM) agent systems have been proposed to automate literature reviews, heterogeneous exposure definitions, effect measures and covariate-adjustment models pose challenges for public health evidence synthesis.

title: Koopman Analysis Reveals Collective Modes Governing Cellular Dynamics
abstract: Living systems are complex nonlinear systems that operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and this nonlinearity makes their dynamics difficult to analyze. Several linearization techniques have been developed to address this problem, but most are local. Koopman operator theory is a powerful alternative that linearizes a system globally. Here we show that it not only achieves global linearization but also reveals collective modes that govern the dynamics of complex, out-of-equilibrium nonlinear systems. Applying the approach to whole-cell dynamical models, we find that these collective modes have physical and biological significance and relate to distinct processes in the cell cycle and in cell-state transitions. Collective and normal modes are widespread in many-body systems, particularly in condensed matter (e.g., magnons, phonons, hydrodynamic modes) and in macromolecular dynamics (e.g., normal mode analysis). By demonstrating that such modes also exist in cell-state transition dynamics, and in non-equilibrium nonlinear systems more generally, we offer a new theoretical-physics perspective on these systems. The collective modes separate into slow and fast modes. Long-term dynamics are governed by a few dominant slow modes that form a slow manifold of much lower dimension than the original state space. Thus, although the cell is a very high-dimensional system, its cell-cycle dynamics ultimately reduce to a low-dimensional space. Each mode comprises the coordinated behavior of groups of genes and reflects the structure of the underlying gene regulatory network. The modes can also be decomposed into terms that behave like damped harmonic oscillators, drawing an analogy between the modes of a nonlinear system and the normal modes of many-body systems. Finally, our analysis suggests that the dominant modes are closely associated with biological processes in the cell cycle, including mitosis, spindle checkpoint signaling, and DNA replication and repair.

title: Sorting reaction pathways to program alkene skeletons
abstract: Small changes in alkene structure usually mean big changes in synthetic routes. Now, nickel catalysts that sort radical and organometallic pathways can deliver four alkene architectures from related building blocks.

title: Phototunable Solid–Liquid Interfacial Energy via Ion–Electron Coupling
abstract: The solid–liquid interfacial energy governs wetting, adhesion, and friction, yet is commonly regarded as a static property defined by surface chemistry and liquid composition. Here we show that light can reversibly modulate the interfacial energy at chemically invariant semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces by tuning the electrostatic coupling between electronic carriers in the solid and ions in the liquid.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Artificial intelligence-driven sustainable polymers research: a lifecycle-integrated perspective.
abstract: The transition toward sustainable polymers necessitates coordinated optimization across the entire materials life cycle. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly deployed to accelerate polymer discovery, yet progress in molecular design, processing and recycling is commonly assessed within individual stages. This review critically examines the shift from single-stage property prediction toward a lifecycle-integrated AI framework.

title: Bayesian Physics-Informed Neural Networks Embedded in Finite Element Analysis: A Probabilistic Digital Twin for Reliability-Based Design of FDM Polymer Components
abstract: Digital twin technology presents revolutionary possibilities for additive manufacturing, but current applications are limited to deterministic forecasting that does not capture manufacturing uncertainties. This study introduces a probabilistic digital twin system that uses machine learning and finite element analysis in two synergistic innovations. First, a Bayesian physics-informed neural network predicts material properties as Abaqus input with quantified uncertainty by embedding Euler-Bernoulli beam theory within a Monte Carlo dropout architecture.

title: Tuning the Electrode Interfacial Microenvironment in Nontraditional Water Electrolysis: Insights From Direct Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: Nontraditional water electrolysis offers a promising route for sustainable green hydrogen production using alternative water resources. Among these systems, direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) provides a representative platform for investigating electrode interfacial challenges, particularly chloride corrosion at the anode and insulative mineral precipitation at the cathode. Many existing studies focus on isolated component design, often struggling to bridge the critical disconnect between idealized kinetic activity and practical operational durability.

title: Exploring candidate molecular links between acetamiprid-related targets and osteosarcoma-associated signatures using network toxicology, transcriptomic analyses, and in vitro validation.
abstract: Acetamiprid (ACE) has been implicated not only in bone metabolic disorders but also in the development of various cancers. Nevertheless, its role in osteosarcoma (OS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, molecular docking, single-cell analysis, machine learning, and preliminary in vitro experiments to explore potential links between ACE-related targets and OS-associated signatures. We identified 219 ACE-related targets and 3299 OS-associated genes, including 62 overlapping candidates.

title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
abstract: Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.

title: Secondary-Shell Phosphorus Engineering of Fe Single-Atom Catalysts for Efficient Electro-Fenton Oxidation
abstract: Selective oxygen reduction for efficient in situ hydroxyl radical (·OH) generation underpins cathodic heterogeneous electro-Fenton (CHEF) technology but remains challenging because catalysts must simultaneously promote H2O2 generation and its rapid activation. Here, we report a waste-to-catalyst strategy that upcycles lithium extraction slag from spent LiFePO4 batteries into a phosphorus-modulated Fe single-atom catalyst (Fe-PNC). Fe-PNC achieves over 95% tetracycline degradation within 30 min under neutral conditions and exhibits broad applicability toward diverse emerging contaminants.

title: Integrating machine learning and molecular docking analysis reveals the molecular network associated with tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common primary liver malignancies worldwide and represents a major global health burden. Increasing evidence suggests that environmental pollutants may contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis. Tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCPP) is a widely used organophosphate flame retardant. Current studies have clearly demonstrated that TDCPP possesses genotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and carcinogenic potential. However, the molecular mechanisms linking TDCPP exposure to HCC remain unclear.

title: BrainRoute integrates machine learning prediction with community-driven verification of blood-brain barrier permeability
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective barrier that restricts the entry of many therapeutic agents into the brain. The lack of efficient methods for BBB permeability research and data management remains a significant challenge for central nervous system drug-development pipelines. Although BBB permeability data are available from multiple open sources, few platforms integrate these datasets with molecular exploration, predictive tools, and a structured process for community-supported data verification.

title: Predictive modeling of photoactivation, diffusion and adsorption in cell - The case of the optogenetic CRY2-CIBN system
abstract: Strategies combining optogenetics and careful spatiotemporal control of photoactivation are highly promising to decipher the dynamical network of biochemical reactions taking place at the m scale in living cells. To improve the spatial resolution of such methods, the roles of various molecular processes, such as photochemical reactions, diffusion and interactions, need to be understood and quantifed. In this article we develop a minimal and realistic model to describe photoactivation, diffusion and surface-binding of optogenetic probes and validate it thanks to experimental results obtained with a CRY2-CIBN system. A theoretical description of optogenetic activation is implemented, based on the photophysics of CRY2 and on its binding kinetics to the membrane through light-dependent heterodimerization with its partner, CIBN. The cell cytosol is described as a closed reservoir of activable CRY2 molecules. Then, a series of photoactivation pulses of a focused laser beam are applied to activate CRY2 proteins, driving their relocalization to the CIBN molecules anchored at the plasma membrane. We examine both the recruitment rate and the spatial distribution of CRY2 molecules recruited after illumination with either propagative or evanescent light. We have estimated numerical values for the corresponding parameters and put into evidence the key role of the optical saturation of photoactivation. These findings establish a framework to further improve spatial control in optogenetic experiments.

title: Polymer overlap and the organization of enzyme activity in crowded solutions
abstract: Macromolecular crowding shapes biochemical reactions in subtle ways, yet a general framework connecting enzyme activity to the physical properties of polymeric crowders remains elusive. Here we show that polymer scaling concepts provide a common framework to organize the effects of crowding on enzyme activity. Using dextran as a model crowder and fluorescence measurements extending beyond the initial-rate regime, we measure the time course of product formation upon peptide hydrolysis by a representative protease. Time-dependent analysis with a reversible kinetic model yields an inferred equilibrium constant whose dependence on dextran concentration collapses onto a common exponential curve after rescaling by a molecular-weight-dependent concentration. We show that the latter displays the same scaling law as the overlap concentration expected for branched dextran, linking quantitatively the reaction response to a fundamental property of polymer solutions. The common behaviour breaks down for the largest dextran at concentrations well above this scale, identifying the limits of the common scaling behaviour. Altogether, these findings suggest that polymer overlap is a general organizing principle for interpreting biochemical kinetics in polymer-crowded solutions.

title: GPU handling of OPC water in GROMACS: validation by protein folding and a 1.6-fold speed-up
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is one of the core computational methods of the life sciences, used to study protein folding, receptor activation and drug binding in atomic detail. The timescales it can reach depend on speed, and running each step entirely on a graphics processing unit (GPU) is now essential for fast simulation. Optimal Point Charge (OPC) water, recommended for the ff19SB protein force field, carries its negative charge on a virtual site, and in GROMACS 2026.3 virtual sites prevent the coordinate update from running on the GPU. The GROMACS developers have recently added GPU handling of virtual sites to the development version as an experimental feature. Whether simulations run in this way agree with the established CPU calculation has to be measured, and no such test has been reported over microseconds or in a membrane-protein system of production size. We compared a modified build that handles OPC sites within the GPU update (Optimized) with the official release (Reference). The two builds placed the charge site with the same error (2.3 x 10^-7 nm) and gave relative force differences below 10^-6. In five matched pairs of 5-microsecond simulations, the Trp-cage miniprotein folded with both builds (three of five Reference and five of five Optimized runs; P = 0.44), and the folded ensembles matched. Both builds reproduced the density, diffusion coefficient, dielectric constant and second hydration shell that distinguish OPC from TIP3P water. In a 166,826-atom membrane system of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, residue hydration agreed between the builds (r = 0.99), and Optimized ran 1.57-1.66 times as fast as tuned Reference on two GPUs, with 87-97% of the time saved coming from moving the coordinate update to the GPU. In these tests, GPU handling of OPC sites gave a substantial speed gain with no sign of altered physical behaviour.

title: A recombinant expression system for the Variant Surface Glycoproteins enables structural elucidation of challenging classes of trypanosome proteins
abstract: The African Trypanosome (Trypanosoma brucei) persists in the mammalian host by periodically altering its surface coat with antigenically distinct versions of the Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG). This process is called antigenic variation and produces repeated cycles of immune clearance and parasite VSG switching, leading to high morbidity and mortality in the absence of chemotherapeutic intervention. Elucidating how variant VSGs evade immune clearance is thus central to understanding trypanosomiasis. Progress in studying the large repertoire of thousands of VSG proteins has been hindered by the challenge of producing these coat proteins. Here we report the use of suspension HEK293 cells for this purpose, a system with robust yields that preserves many key elements of VSG structure and post-translational modifications, verified by expressing, purifying, and determining the crystal structures of the well-characterized proteins VSG2 and VSG3. We then applied this heterologous expression system to the production of several VSGs that had failed to express natively in T. brucei, including truncated VSG-Related Proteins (VRPs) from T. brucei and VSGs from T. vivax. This allowed for the determination of the structures of the T. brucei VRP VSG1619 as well as the VSG F9WSW0 from Trypanosoma vivax (T. vivax). The structure of VSG1619 shows similarities to the upper-lobe structures of B-class VSGs, but the monomers do not assemble into either the typical A-class dimer or B-class trimer in solution or in the crystals. The structure of T. vivax F9WSW0 is notable as a divergent member of the Class-A group that was developed from structures of T. brucei VSGs, with a canonical dimer but differences in fold, disulfide placement, and N-linked glycosylation. The described expression system provides additional insight into the family of VRPs and opens the door to general progress with the VSGs of more divergent trypanosome species through recombinant protein production.

title: Molecular Conformer Sampling Beyond Generations
abstract: Sampling the low-energy conformational states available to a molecule is a fundamental problem in computational chemistry and drug discovery, since molecular properties and downstream design decisions depend on the relevant three-dimensional geometries rather than on a single structure. Recent diffusion and flow-based generative models can efficiently sample conformer candidates from molecular graphs, but under a fixed output budget their samples do not cover the full set of relevant conformational states of a molecule, while practical benchmarks and downstream applications require a small ensemble that is both diverse and physically plausible. We present a post-generation selection framework that turns candidate pools from frozen, pre-trained generators into compact conformer ensembles without any retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying generator. The framework offers two selectors that share the same candidate pool and the same learned reference-likelihood classifier: CovSelect, a coverage-maximizing selector that greedily reaches as many distinct reference states as the pool allows, and RefSelect, a tunable selector that trades some of that coverage for higher precision and, at its balanced setting, matches or exceeds strong generative baselines on both measures at once. On the full GEOM-DRUGS test set, CovSelect reaches 91.33% mean recall (98.36% median), outperforming every raw generator we compare against, and RefSelect at its balanced setting exceeds the strongest raw baseline, DMT-L, on both recall and precision. Finally, across several out of distribution benchmarks (QMugs, pepconf, and Platinum), CovSelect substantially outperforms all raw generative baselines in recall and precision.

title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks
abstract: Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO 2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four ‘AI-dreamt’ MOFs.

title: Machine learning integrated simulation of thermal convective flow dynamics of radiative nanomaterial using Buongiorno model.
abstract: Present study deals with numerical and predictive analysis of Maxwell fluid flow over a permeable surface. Various physical phenomena are taken under consideration such as double diffusion, first order chemical reaction and heat source in heat and mass equations. Proposed model resolved with help of Lie transformations. Transformed ODEs were resolved using the well-known numerical algorithm Bvp4c in MATLAB, and datasets were created for application of machine learning algorithm (i.e. Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm). Furthermore, the uniformity and stability of the approach were ensured.

title: Electrothermal Mapping: A Methodology for Decoupling Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Integrative network toxicology and genetic association analyses prioritize FASN as a potential molecular link between cigarette smoke exposure and male infertility.
abstract: Male infertility (MIF) is a complex reproductive disorder influenced by genetic, lifestyle, and environmental factors. Cigarette smoke (CS) contains numerous reproductive toxicants and has been associated with impaired semen quality and fertility. However, the molecular mechanisms linking CS exposure to MIF remain unclear. Representative toxic constituents of CS were selected based on previous studies, and multiple databases were integrated to identify CS associated targets, which were intersected with MIF associated genes to obtain CS-MIF common targets.

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

title: Influence of Ce Substitution on the Thermoelectric Properties of the Incommensurate Misfit-Layered Compound (La0.94S)1.14(NbS2)
abstract: In the present work, the thermoelectric (TE) properties of p-type lanthanum-deficient misfit-layered sulfide (La0.94S)1.14(NbS2) were investigated by substituting Ce into the partially occupied lanthanum site. The pristine and Ce-substituted solid solution samples crystallize in the incommensurate composite layered structure with the orthorhombic (3 + 1)D superspace group F’m2m(q,0,0)00s, consisting of alternating La0.94−xCex☐yS and NbS2 slabs stacked on each other along the c-axis (□ symbolizes the cationic vacancies).

title: MammoInsight: A Unified Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Mammography Analysis
abstract: Background Mammography interpretation requires simultaneous assessment of multiple clinical attributes such as cancer status, breast density, BI-RADS score, abnormality type, and molecular subtype. The existing AI systems generally address these tasks in isolation, limiting clinical utility and generalizability. title: Inverse Design of Polyarylate Nanofiber-Enabled Basalt Scale Nanocomposite Insulating Paper for High Dielectric Reliability via Finite Element-Guided Machine Learning
abstract: The dielectric reliability of polymer-based insulating paper critically depends on whether its structure-property relationships can be predicted and programmatically tuned. However, most dielectric papers are still developed through empirical trial-and-error, which limits precise design and efficient optimization toward target performance metrics. title: Electropositive Site Engineering via Ordered Intermetallic Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution: From M 2P to Zr2 M 12P7 ( M = Ni, Co, Fe)
abstract: Doping and alloying is a common strategy to modify the electronic structures of transition metal phosphide (M–P) electrocatalyst to improve their performance. However, the disorder associated with doping and alloying leads to a distribution of local crystal and electronic structures, thus complicating understanding of structure-property relationships. In turn, ordered ternary A–M–P phases with distinct crystallographic sites for each element represent tunable single-site catalysts given their diversity in compositions and structures.

title: Cation Effects on the Electro-oxidation of Alcohols Are Not Mediated Solely by Their Interactions with Adsorbed OH
abstract: In this work, we deconvolute the impact of electrolyte cations on the electro-oxidation of glycerol (GOR) on Pt. UV–vis reflectograms reveal that the presence of glycerol inverts and enhances the magnitude of cation effects on Pt oxidation. A cation-dependent glycerol diffusion coefficient was then identified using 1H-DOSY-NMR, evidencing that cation-induced trends in GOR reactivity are not controlled by the rate of diffusion of glycerol to the Pt surface, and that smaller cations interact more strongly with glycerol than larger ones. The rates of partial oxidation of glycerol to adsorbed carbon monoxide (COad) and of COad oxidation, measured as a function of cation identity using time-resolved ATR-SEIRAS, suggest that global cation-induced trends in GOR activity are driven mainly by reaction pathways that do not involve COad. We emphasize though that this conclusion remains supported primarily by indirect evidence and logical exclusion rather than direct observation. In any case, the results presented here imply that interactions between electrolyte cations and adsorbed oxygenated species (AOS) alone cannot explain the cation-induced trends in electrocatalytic behavior observed.

title: Confronting the imperfections of adeno-associated virus gene therapy vectors: defining genomic integrity and characterization methods.
abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors are the predominant modality for delivering gene therapies to treat genetic diseases across multiple organ types. Capsid and genomic payload designs ultimately define the optimal efficacious dose that is potent and safe. Vector doses are dependent on calculated titers, which are typically defined by the abundance of encapsidated vector genomes detected in a purified production batch. Over the last ten years, advanced sequencing methods have been developed to characterize individual molecular species that are packaged into rAAV particles.
venue: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

title: Composition-Driven Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
abstract: Structure–activity relationships built on structure-derived descriptors are a dominant paradigm in catalyst screening. However, this structure-driven framework scales poorly to multimetallic systems, where active sites are heterogeneous, dynamically reconstruct under operating conditions, and require extensive structural enumeration and system-specific descriptor engineering. Here, we introduce a composition-driven screening strategy for multimetallic catalysts using feature construction inspired by the virtual crystal approximation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Ionic waves drive fluid flow by inducing spatiotemporal porosity variations in the brain interstitial space
abstract: We develop a model of interstitial fluid (ISF) dynamics in the brain driven by traveling ionic waves. The cortex is modeled as a 2D porous sheet with an absorbent matrix. A prescribed 10% sinusoidal porosity variation induces mean flow of O(1) {micro}m/s, even without an imposed pressure gradient. Including perivascular spaces (PVSs) increases the velocity and pressure gradient, and yields volumetric flux through arterial and venous PVSs, with maximum magnitude of 2 x 10-2 {micro}L min-1 mm-1. We show analytically, in the large-wavelength limit, that the porosity variation enters the pressure field as first- and second-order corrections. We then simulate a physiologically realistic spreading depolarization (SD) wave, finding that the induced porosity variation raises the mean ISF pressure to 4 mmHg, which falls to -0.7 mmHg during recovery. SD yields a peak velocity of O(10-2) {micro}m/s and a peak flux of 3 x 10-3 {micro}L min-1 mm-1, and transiently stalls the PVS-driven flow. Although the SD wave produces a larger porosity change than the prescribed wave, it evolves slowly and drives weaker flow.

title: canSAR 2026-an update to the public drug discovery knowledgebase
abstract: canSAR (https://cansar.ai) serves as the world's largest public platform for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It serves as an exploration and hypothesis generation platform for drug discovery through (i) fully integrating large, multidisciplinary data from public resources, as well as bespoke curated data, creating a connected, navigable drug discovery knowledge map; and (ii) applying a suite of machine learning and AI tools to generate novel insights.

title: DriverDBv5: a multi-omics integration database for cancer driver gene research
abstract: Cancer is driven by alterations across multiple molecular layers, but whether multi-omics drivers carry prognostic weight has received little systematic attention. DriverDBv5 (https://driverdb.bioinfomics.org/) extends DriverDB from driver identification to prognostic evaluation. It has been expanded to 187 cohorts, 43 862 patients, and 129 655 samples, with 154 cohorts from non-TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) repositories reconciled by a generalized multi-omics barcode.

title: Machine learning-assisted Ce/Co metal-organic framework-based fluorescence/electrochemical dual-modal sensor for sensitive detection of ochratoxin A.
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) is a highly toxic mycotoxin that poses serious risks to food safety and human health. Herein, a rationally designed cerium-cobalt metal-organic framework (Ce/Co-PTC-MOF) was developed as a dual-mode opto-electrochemical sensing platform for rapid, selective, and bioreceptor-free detection of OTA. The flower-like Ce/Co-PTC-MOF efficiently quenches rhodamine B (Rh-B) fluorescence through electrostatic interactions, while the redox-active Ce/Co centers enabled direct OTA recognition without biological receptors.

title: Hydrogeological Modeling of Permeation Grouting: Application to Silicate Grouting from Injection through Degradation
abstract: No existing modeling framework seamlessly captures the multi-stage progression of sodium silicate grouting, from initial injection through long-term chemical evolution, at the field scale. We present a modeling framework that integrates numerical simulation with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) neural network to bridge this gap. The numerical model simulates grout transport during injection and implicitly tracks the transient evolution of soil properties as the gel hardens. Once the injection is complete, a low-permeability barrier forms, controlling groundwater inflow.

title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
abstract: The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Optimizing environmental conditions for PALM imaging of the nuclear pore complex labeled with the photoconvertible fluorescent protein mEos4b.
abstract: Green-to-red photoconvertible fluorescent proteins (PCFPs) are smart fluorophores used in several nanoscopy approaches based on single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM). To optimize the achievable spatial resolution and facilitate molecular counting in these approaches, PCFPs should deliver a high effective labeling efficiency (ELE). Here, to evaluate the ELE provided by mEos4b, a performant PCFP, we designed a constitutive Nup96-mEos4b protein fusion in the nuclear pore complex (NPC) of U2OS cells, and performed PhotoActivated Localization Microscopy (PALM) imaging of NPCs in fixed cells under different environmental conditions. We find that removal of oxygen improves the ELE by more than 20%. Overall, using HEPES as buffer in deuterated and deoxygenated water delivers the highest quality PALM images of NPCs labeled with mEos4b. These conditions should be beneficial for quantitative PALM or Minimal Fluorescence Photon Fluxes Microscopy (Minflux) experiments in fixed cells. We propose a photophysical scheme that accounts for the observed improvements in the absence of oxygen.

title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields
abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein–ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. Whether and when these challenges demand more sophisticated physical models has remained an open question. Here, we address it through a systematic comparison of the polarizable OPLS5 and fixed-charge OPLS4 force fields within an alchemical FEP framework, across three RNA-ligand systems of increasing complexity: (i) a fully resolved PreQ1 riboswitch with native-like fragments; (ii) a partially resolved PreQ1 riboswitch with synthetic ligands; and (iii) a group II intron with metal-coordinating inhibitors. We find that preparatory molecular dynamics is a crucial determinant of accuracy, with even short nanosecond-scale equilibration substantially improving ligand ranking by allowing the system to access functionally relevant conformations. Explicit polarizability becomes decisive precisely where the physics is hardest─recovering native-like architectures from incomplete structures, and converging charge-changing transformations at metal-coordination sites─while offering only marginal gains for well-resolved, structurally stable complexes. Together, these results define the conditions under which physical rigor is justified despite its higher computational cost and chart the potential for failures that still constrain free-energy methods applied to RNA. More broadly, our results offer a transferable framework for deploying physics-based affinity prediction against RNA target classes.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: All-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries are a next-generation high-energy-density solution for energy storage. Here catholyte/cathode interfaces are found to be as important as transport tortuosity in thick sulfur cathodes, and an areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2 is demonstrated at a stack pressure of 15 MPa and sulfur loading of 6.1 mg cm−2.

title: Multiscale Topological Transcriptomic Analysis for Alzheimer’s Disease Drug Repurposing
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder driven by multifactorial molecular mechanisms, which severely limit the efficacy of current therapeutic interventions. To accelerate the discovery of novel treatments, we propose a comprehensive computational framework integrating transcriptomic analysis, topological network characterization, machine learning (ML), and structure-based evaluation. By analyzing eight independent AD transcriptomic datasets, we constructed protein–protein interaction networks and implemented a multiscale topological differentiation strategy based on persistent homology and persistent spectral theory. This approach quantified the topological importance of each gene, prioritizing 67 nonredundant key genes. To bridge target identification with drug screening, we mapped these genes to the ChEMBL database, yielding 4,493 bioactivity records across five primary targets. We evaluated three ML algorithms across diverse molecular representations, including two natural language processing-derived molecular embeddings and a conventional molecular fingerprint. Deploying these predictive models for large-scale virtual screening of the DrugBank database yielded several promising repurposing candidates. Subsequent molecular docking against the target proteins GLP1R and CASP1 generated predicted binding poses for selected compounds. Physicochemical profiling identified differences relevant to their further assessment, although these computational results do not establish binding stability, pharmacokinetic suitability, or safety. This study not only identifies viable therapeutic candidates for AD but also provides a scalable, generalizable pipeline for target prioritization and drug discovery applicable to other complex human diseases.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: The person behind the scientist
abstract: Matteo Seita and Mengying Liu discuss their reflections as organizers of The Past Metallurgists Society lecture series, where scientists meet to share stories of distinguished metallurgists from the past.
